title: Spritz Notes: meta-learning, ops, and practical hacks from recent readings/conference
content:
Quick context: collecting small takeaways from 3 papers + 2 panels at the workshop. Not polished; a fast brain dump for follow-up experiments.

Top-level goal: look for things we can prototype in Redwood Optimize / runtime in the next 4 weeks. Emphasis: low-risk infra experiments that give observable perf or cost wins, or provide diagnostic signals for regressions.

-- Highlights / one-liners I want to remember:
- Meta-learning for prompt adapters: cheap adapter-initialization seems to cut few-shot prompt shrink cost by ~20% if you can pretrain adapter initializations on domain distributions. Feels promising for Dedicated customers with repetitive domain patterns.
- Online adapter warmups: treat adapter state like a KV cache: persist last-N adapters per-customer and warm them on new request bursts. Could be layered into our prefix-caching mechanism.
- Paper X (arXiv 2601.01234): gradient-based meta-learners for short-context adaptation. Key insight: inner-loop is cheap when adapter is <1M params; outer-loop provides good generalization. Implementation note: training schedule uses episodes sampled from domain clusters — we could leverage our dataset tags to create episodes.
- Practical ops trick from panel: instrument an "adapter mismatch" metric — how often the selected adapter (or model variant) produces token distribution shifts vs baseline. Correlates with perceived hallucination spikes.

-- Notes from readings (ordered by priority)
1) Meta-Adapters: lightweight domain adapters for prompt cost reduction (paper + code)
- method: adapter modules inserted in residual blocks, trained via MAML-like outer loop on domain episodes.
- reported wins: 15-30% token reduction in prompting per-domain (because adapter encodes domain context and reduces need for long few-shot prefixes).
- caveats: needs curated episodes; brittle if domain drift is high.
- idea: try a 3-month pilot on one CS-heavy customer (support transcripts). Create episodes by sampling threads tagged with product area.
2) KV-compression blog (link above) - heuristics for compressing KV stores with quick lossy transforms
- approach: chunk-level PCA + delta-encoding + quantize-to-8-bit for cold entries.
- cost/latency: extra CPU for decompress but helped cold-start cost 2x on an internal bench.
- thought: for Dedicated pools where we keep large per-customer caches, compress cold prefixes to save GPU memory. Can fall back to raw when latency budget allows.
3) Online meta-learning for adapters (workshop talk)
- speaker: Dr. Liao — demoed a streaming inner-loop that updates adapter with synthetic gradients (no full backprop) on high-confidence predictions.
- risk: update noise leads to drift. Benefit: fast personalization without full retrain.
- ops guardrail: require "confidence momentum" check and a decay schedule; put changes behind canary traffic.

-- Conference panel notes (2 short panels)
- Panel A: "Personalization at scale"
- theme: caching vs model adaptation. Consensus: caching is cheaper but brittle; adapters + small updates offer better long tail coverage.
- ops takeaway: combine both — cache frequent prefixes, use adapters to generalize beyond cached items.
- Panel B: "Costs, SLOs, and graceful degradation"
- theme: smart fallbacks critical. Use model-variant routing + prompt shrinking heuristics.
- ops takeaway: add "token budget per-request" feature that circuit-breaks to compressed-response model if burst budget exceeded.

-- Immediate followups (work items / todo)
- [x] Write experiment brief for adapter warmup + prefix-cache combo (Felix) — due 2026-05-22.
- [ ] Create synthetic episodes from customer support dataset (ticket TKT-2981) to pretrain mini-adapter (owner: Asha).
- [ ] Add instrumentation for adapter-selection drift metric (owner: Noah) — prototype in Redwood Console as a per-route chart.
- [ ] Bench KV-compression on a 4GB cache snapshot (owner: Felix) — measure decompress CPU cost vs memory saved.

-- Design sketches / how this plugs into Redwood runtime
- Serving flow (fast sketch): request arrives -> policy selects model variant -> check per-customer adapter store -> if adapter present and warm: inject adapter; else if adapter cold: route to warmup pool (micro-burst to initialize + small prefetch of likely prefixes).
- Warmup policy: throttle warmups by queue length and only allow N warmups concurrently per-customer. If warmups exceed budget, route to compressed-response variant.
- Metrics to capture:
- adapter_warm_hits (counter), adapter_warm_latency (p50/p95), adapter_mismatch_rate (ratio of per-token KL to baseline model), kv_compress_ratio (mem_before / mem_after)

-- Risks / open questions I keep in head:
- Privacy: storing adapters that encode customer signals may be sensitive. Need to treat adapter artifacts as customer data. KMS & retention policy needed.
- Drift: online updates could cause silent drift. Must have rollback and regression detection (prompt-sets evals).
- Complexity: more moving parts in routing; need clear canaries and opt-outs for customers who want simpler behavior.

-- Quick experiment plan (2-week spike)
Week 1:
- implement toy adapter insertion in a small transformer (on CPU Docker)
- create episode sampling script from CS transcripts (1000 episodes)
- pretrain small adapter init (50k steps)
Week 2:
- integrate warmup-only path in local runtime (no infra changes)
- run microbench: token cost comparisons for 100 synthetic queries with/without adapter
- dashboard: add adapter_mismatch metric to dev console for these runs

-- Notes-to-self style loose fragments:
- Would an adapter fingerprint (hash of adapter weights) help correlate downstream failures? probably yes. add as label in traces.
- Consider small A/B test: route 5% traffic to adapter path for a single customer. Make alert if mismatch_rate > 0.15.
- If pretraining adapters works, offer as an "Optimize" chargeable service: per-domain adapter pretrain + deployment. Pricing thought: one-off train + monthly storage.

References / links I want to read fully:
- arXiv:2601.01234 (meta-adapters)
- KV compression blog post (link above)
- Workshop slides: Liao "online adapter warmup" (slack thread pinned)

End of dump. Revisit after initial bench.
